subject: Biology
description: Viruses — structure, classification, replication, common viral diseases, antiviral drugs, COVID-19, vaccines.

questions.stem: Viruses are NOT considered living organisms because they:

options.option_text: Are too tiny to be seen at all

questions.explanation: VIRUSES are 'AT THE EDGE OF LIFE' — they have GENETIC MATERIAL (DNA or RNA), but they CANNOT METABOLIZE, CANNOT REPRODUCE on their own, and CANNOT MAINTAIN HOMEOSTASIS without infecting a host cell. Outside a host, they exist as INERT PARTICLES (virions). KEY FEATURES: (1) Size: ~20-300 nm (much smaller than bacteria; need electron microscopes). (2) STRUCTURE: nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) + protein coat (CAPSID) + sometimes a lipid envelope. (3) HOST-DEPENDENT: must HIJACK host cell's ribosomes, enzymes, energy to replicate. CLASSIFICATION: (a) DNA viruses: smallpox, HPV, herpes, hepatitis B. (b) RNA viruses: flu, HIV, SARS-CoV-2, polio, Ebola, dengue. (c) RETROVIRUSES (reverse-transcribing): HIV, HTLV. (d) BACTERIOPHAGES — viruses that infect bacteria. SCIENTIFIC NAMES — DISCOVERED BY: Dmitri Ivanovsky (1892, tobacco mosaic virus), Martinus Beijerinck (1898, coined 'virus'). NOBEL: many for virus discoveries — most recently 2020 (Hepatitis C). PYQ FREQUENCY: virus-vs-bacteria distinction is a top NEET, SSC, JEE biology MCQ — 1-2× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests fundamental life-criteria.

questions.stem: Which of these diseases is caused by a VIRUS?
questions.explanation: AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome) is caused by HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus), a RETROVIRUS first identified in 1983 by Luc Montagnier (Nobel 2008). HIV destroys CD4+ T-helper cells, weakening immunity. TRANSMISSION: blood, sexual contact, mother-to-child. TREATMENT: ART (Antiretroviral Therapy) controls but doesn't cure. INDIA: ~24 lakh PLHIV (people living with HIV) as of 2024; NACO (National AIDS Control Organisation) leads programs. OTHER MAJOR VIRAL DISEASES (memorize): (1) COVID-19 — SARS-CoV-2 (RNA virus, 2019-present). (2) Influenza — flu virus (RNA). (3) Common cold — rhinovirus, coronavirus. (4) Measles, mumps, rubella (MMR vaccines). (5) Polio — poliovirus (India eradicated 2014). (6) Smallpox — variola virus (eradicated globally 1980). (7) Hepatitis A, B, C, D, E. (8) Dengue, Chikungunya, Zika — RNA arboviruses (mosquito-borne). (9) Rabies — Lyssavirus (100% fatal once symptoms appear). (10) Ebola, Lassa fever — hemorrhagic fevers. CONTRAST: bacterial = TB, cholera, plague; protozoan = malaria, amoebic dysentery; fungal = ringworm, athlete's foot. PYQ FREQUENCY: causative-organism MCQs in CGL, NEET, IBPS GA — 1-2 per cycle.

questions.stem: The protein coat that surrounds a virus's genetic material is called the:
questions.explanation: CAPSID = the PROTEIN COAT surrounding a virus's nucleic acid (DNA or RNA). It's made up of repeating PROTEIN SUBUNITS called CAPSOMERES. The capsid + the nucleic acid together form the NUCLEOCAPSID. STRUCTURAL TYPES: (1) HELICAL — rod-shaped (e.g., tobacco mosaic virus). (2) ICOSAHEDRAL — 20-faced polyhedron (e.g., adenovirus, polio). (3) COMPLEX — like bacteriophages (head-tail-fibers, T4 phage). FUNCTIONS of CAPSID: (a) Protects nucleic acid from enzymes/UV. (b) Helps in attachment to host cells. (c) Determines antigenic identity (immune recognition). ENVELOPED VIRUSES: have an additional LIPID BILAYER OUTSIDE the capsid (stolen from the host membrane during budding). Examples: HIV, influenza, herpes, COVID-SARS-CoV-2, hepatitis B. NON-ENVELOPED (naked) viruses: polio, adenovirus, rhinovirus. ENVELOPED viruses are usually MORE FRAGILE in environment but evade immunity better; non-enveloped are HARDIER (resist soap, drying). SOAP destroys the lipid envelope of COVID-19 — that's why HAND-WASHING WORKS. PYQ FREQUENCY: virus structure parts are NEET, NCERT Class 11 staple.

questions.stem: Which scientist first discovered viruses while studying tobacco mosaic disease?
questions.explanation: DMITRI IVANOVSKY (1892, Russia) — discovered that tobacco mosaic disease was caused by an infectious agent SMALLER than bacteria; passed through bacterial filters. He didn't quite recognize it as a NEW kind of organism. MARTINUS BEIJERINCK (1898, Netherlands) — repeated Ivanovsky's experiments and called the agent 'CONTAGIUM VIVUM FLUIDUM' (contagious living fluid), and coined the term 'VIRUS' (Latin for 'poison'). FIRST VIRUS to be CRYSTALLIZED: Tobacco Mosaic Virus, by Wendell Stanley (1935, Nobel 1946). FIRST ANIMAL VIRUS: foot-and-mouth virus (Loeffler & Frosch, 1898). FIRST HUMAN VIRUS: yellow fever virus (Walter Reed et al., 1901). FIRST BACTERIOPHAGE: Frederick Twort (1915), Felix d'Herelle (1917). KEY VIROLOGY MILESTONES: (a) 1957 — interferons discovered. (b) 1953 — DNA structure (Watson-Crick). (c) 1983 — HIV identified. (d) 2003 — SARS coronavirus. (e) 2019 — SARS-CoV-2. JENNER (1796): smallpox vaccine, but he didn't know it was a virus — used cowpox material. PASTEUR (1885): rabies vaccine — also didn't fully understand viruses. KOCH: bacteria, not viruses (but 'Koch's postulates' were later applied). PYQ FREQUENCY: 'father of virology' MCQ in NEET, CGL.

questions.stem: SARS-CoV-2, the virus causing COVID-19, contains its genetic material in the form of:
questions.explanation: SARS-CoV-2 (Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2) — has POSITIVE-SENSE SINGLE-STRANDED RNA (+ssRNA) genome of ~30,000 nucleotides — one of the LARGEST RNA virus genomes. STRUCTURE: spherical (~120 nm), spike (S) glycoprotein on surface — gives 'crown-like' (corona = crown) appearance under microscope. KEY PROTEINS: (a) S (spike) — binds ACE2 receptor on human cells. (b) E (envelope). (c) M (membrane). (d) N (nucleocapsid). VARIANTS of CONCERN: Alpha (UK, Sept 2020), Beta (SA), Gamma (Brazil), Delta (India, 2021 second wave catastrophe), Omicron (SA, Nov 2021), and many sub-variants. INDIA TIMELINE: First case 30 Jan 2020 (Kerala student returning from Wuhan). National lockdown 25 March 2020. Vaccination drive started 16 Jan 2021 (Covishield + Covaxin). Pandemic officially ended (WHO) 5 May 2023. WHY +ssRNA matters: directly translatable by host ribosomes (acts as mRNA). NEGATIVE-SENSE RNA viruses (flu, rabies) need to first transcribe complementary RNA. RNA viruses MUTATE faster than DNA (no proofreading) — explains rapid emergence of variants. PYQ FREQUENCY: COVID-related virology in NEET 2022-2026 papers; SSC GA 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which disease was the FIRST in human history to be eradicated globally through vaccination?
questions.explanation: SMALLPOX — caused by VARIOLA virus — was declared OFFICIALLY ERADICATED by WHO on 8 MAY 1980 — the FIRST and ONLY human disease eradicated globally. VACCINE PIONEER: EDWARD JENNER (1796) noticed milkmaids who had cowpox were immune to smallpox. Used cowpox (vaccinia virus) — origin of word 'VACCINE' (vacca = cow in Latin). LAST NATURAL CASE of smallpox: Ali Maow Maalin, Somalia, 1977. WHY ERADICATION POSSIBLE for smallpox: (1) Only human reservoir (no animal hosts). (2) No long-term carriers. (3) Distinctive symptoms (easy diagnosis). (4) Effective stable vaccine. (5) Lifelong immunity from one infection. POLIO is on the verge — INDIA was certified POLIO-FREE in 2014 (Pulse Polio Programme). Globally, only Pakistan and Afghanistan have wild polio cases as of 2024. RINDERPEST (a cattle disease) was eradicated in 2011 — second disease ever. CHALLENGES for other diseases: animal reservoirs (rabies, malaria), rapid mutation (flu, HIV), no effective vaccine yet (HIV, HCV — though HCV has effective antivirals). VACCINE-PREVENTABLE in INDIA: BCG (TB), OPV (polio), MMR, DPT, HepB, HPV. PYQ FREQUENCY: smallpox-eradication is a perennial NEET, SSC, UPSC fact.

questions.stem: BACTERIOPHAGES are viruses that specifically infect:
questions.explanation: BACTERIOPHAGES (or PHAGES, Greek for 'bacteria-eaters') — viruses that infect and reproduce inside BACTERIA. Discovered by Frederick Twort (1915) and Félix d'Hérelle (1917). STRUCTURE: typically ICOSAHEDRAL HEAD (containing DNA) + TAIL (helical) + TAIL FIBERS (for attachment). The classic T4 PHAGE infects E. coli — looks like a 'lunar-lander' under EM. LIFE CYCLES: (1) LYTIC — phage hijacks bacteria, makes copies, BURSTS the cell (lysis). Within 30 min, hundreds of new phages released. (2) LYSOGENIC — phage DNA integrates into bacterial chromosome (PROPHAGE), passively replicated; can later switch to lytic cycle. PHAGE THERAPY: using phages to kill antibiotic-resistant bacteria — RESURGENT INTEREST due to antibiotic-resistance crisis. Used in Eastern Europe (Georgia's Eliava Institute). USA, EU now studying phage therapy. NUMBERS: phages are the MOST ABUNDANT life forms on Earth — ~10³¹ total, more than all bacteria combined. ECOLOGY: kill ~50% of ocean bacteria daily — major regulator of microbial ecosystems. RECOMBINANT DNA TECH: phage λ (lambda) is a key cloning vector. PYQ FREQUENCY: phage MCQ in NEET, JEE-Adv biology.
